name.text: Calculating exact value of sine theta

questiontext.text:
The angle \(\theta\) lies in Quadrant {@quadrant@} and satisfies (\cos(\theta)={@cos_value@}.\) Determine the exact value of \(\sin(\theta).\)

Give your answer in exact form.

[[input:ans1]]

[[validation:ans1]] [[feedback:prt1]]

generalfeedback.text:
To find the value of \(\sin(\theta)\), use the Pythagorean identity \(\sin^2(\theta)+\cos^2(\theta)=1\).

You are given \(\cos(\theta)={@cos_value@}\). Therefore, \(\sin^2(\theta)=1-\cos^2(\theta)\).

Substituting the given value gives \(\sin^2(\theta)=1-({@cos_value@})^2\).

Taking the square root gives \(\sin(\theta)=\pm\sqrt{1-({@cos_value@})^2}\).

The quadrant determines which sign is required. Sine is positive in Quadrants I and II and negative in Quadrants III and IV.

Since \(\theta\) is in Quadrant {@quadrant@}, the appropriate sign must be selected. Therefore, \(\sin(\theta)={@ta@}\).

Remember: first find the magnitude using \(\sin^2(\theta)+\cos^2(\theta)=1\), and then use the quadrant to determine the sign.

prtpartiallycorrect.text: Your answer is partially correct.

prtincorrect.text: Incorrect answer.

The correct value is \(\sin(\theta)={@ta@}\).
